meta.title: TS-RaMIA · Symbolic Music Membership Auditing
meta.description: Evidence-first research page for TS-RaMIA, a structure-aware membership auditing method for symbolic music generation models.
a11y.audit_flow: A candidate symbolic-music piece is scored by an audited model to test a membership hypothesis
a11y.trap_results: Baseline AUC before and after confounder control

a11y.figure1_alt: Published TS-RaMIA Figure 1 showing data protocol, structural masking, sample-level NLL, debiasing, tail aggregation, and meta-attacker fusion

hero.deck: A structure-aware, debiased audit that asks whether a symbolic music work was used to train a generation model—without turning confounders into false evidence.
hero.boundary: The page separates the research question, method, controlled evidence, negative results, and deployment limits before presenting headline numbers.
audit.title: Can a creator test whether a piece was used to train a music generation model?
audit.hypothesis: H₀: x ∉ Dtrain · H₁: x ∈ Dtrain
audit.decision_note: Then evaluated on a held-out test set
audit.not_body: The output is an audit signal. Rights holders should combine it with provenance, licensing records, metadata, and other supporting evidence.
threat.title: What the auditor can access—and what remains a deployment gap
threat.allowed2: Obtain per-token log-probabilities through teacher forcing
threat.not4: No access to the target training set
threat.gap1: Some commercial APIs do not expose per-token probabilities.
threat.gap3: Those approximations increase query cost and are not the paper’s primary evaluation.
trap.title: Why naïve sequence loss can look convincing for the wrong reason
trap.factor1_body: Longer works contain more opportunities for extreme loss values.
trap.factor2_body: Bar, position, and tempo counts can correlate with the split.
trap.factor3_body: Dense passages change the loss distribution independently of membership.
trap.conclusion: Without confounder control, an apparently successful attack may only be recognizing structural complexity.
insight.title: Leakage is not uniformly distributed across musical tokens
insight.remi: Bar, Position, and Tempo form the structural mask; note, pitch, and velocity tokens have different functions.
insight.abc: Headers before the first body line are excluded. Body-level meter, key, or voice changes remain under the paper’s rules; normalized newlines are not structural tokens.
insight.observe_body: Per-token NLL is the base observation. Tail statistics surface sparse local anomalies that a full-sequence average can dilute.
insight.decision_body: A directed, standardized meta-attacker produces the final score under cross-validation. A single raw NLL is not a membership probability.
pipeline.title: Five stages, one controlled audit score
pipeline.intro: Select a stage to inspect it on the unchanged Figure 1 from the paper.
pipeline.stage1_body: Expose Bar, Position, and Tempo in REMI or body-level structural characters in ABC while excluding formatting artifacts.
pipeline.stage2_body: Teacher forcing records token difficulty across non-overlapping chunks while excluding chunk-initial tokens.
pipeline.stage3_body: Length matching and conditional calibration remove first-order structural-length dependence.
pipeline.stage4_body: Top-k and windowed p95 statistics concentrate sparse evidence at structure-relevant positions.
pipeline.stage5_body: A lightweight, regularized logistic model fuses standardized features under composer-stratified cross-validation.
pipeline.caption: Published Figure 1, extracted from the final PMLR paper without redrawing. The transparent outline is a webpage annotation only.
pipeline.detail1_body: Teacher forcing yields per-token NLL. Non-overlapping chunks exclude each chunk’s initial token because it lacks within-chunk context.
pipeline.detail2_body: Nearest-neighbor length matching and conditional calibration isolate membership evidence from structural length.
pipeline.detail3_body: Three structural top-k scores use k ∈ {32, 64, 128}; three windowed p95 statistics capture local peaks.
pipeline.detail4_body: Optional reverse/hierarchical features complete a nine-dimensional vector when available. Each fold applies z-score normalization before L2-regularized, class-weighted logistic regression.
pipeline.detail5_body: Composer-stratified five-fold cross-validation produces out-of-fold predictions, reducing stylistic leakage between training and evaluation folds.
evidence.title: Inspect the controlled Table 1 results
evidence.intro: This explorer exposes only aggregate results published in PMLR 303. It never produces a sample-level probability.
evidence.controlled_note: Controlled evaluation view; not a per-sample probability.
evidence.table1_caption: Table 1 · REMI Transformer results. AUC includes 95% confidence intervals.
evidence.figure2_caption: Rendered from the final paper and cropped only around the figure boundary. It is not a reconstructed curve and no values are digitized from it. Final Table 1 is the numerical reporting source.
view_note.matched: Controls structural-token count through nearest-neighbor pairing.
view_note.calibrated: Removes first-order dependence on log structural length.
lowfpr.title: Why low false-positive rates matter
lowfpr.body1: False accusations are costly, so rights-holder audits need evidence at a strict false-positive budget—not AUC alone.
lowfpr.body2: At the 1% FPR operating point, the length-matched fusion result detects 14.6% of true members. That is recall at a fixed error budget, not the false-positive rate and not detection of most training samples.
lowfpr.body3: The decision threshold must be selected on a development split, never tuned on the test set.
ablation.title: What failed—and what that taught us
ablation.caption: Table 2 · Length-matched ablations
ablation.finding1_body: It balances variance against signal dilution; it was not chosen arbitrarily.
ablation.finding2_title: Windowed p95 adds a small lift
ablation.finding2_body: Local peaks help, but they do not replace structural top-k aggregation.
ablation.finding3_body: Performance near the full-piece result argues against piece length being the only signal.
ablation.negative1_body: Score inversion can recover approximately 0.68, but only if orientation is known in advance. It is not a usable attack as-is.
ablation.negative2_body: With 314 non-member samples, fitting was unstable and did not outperform simpler top-k aggregation.
transfer.title: Does the trend survive a different symbolic representation?
transfer.boundary: NotaGen was pretrained on an external ABC corpus, while MAESTRO-derived ABC is held out. This supports a cross-representation trend under distribution shift—not a direct in-distribution replication.
checkpoint.title: Membership risk accumulates as training progresses
checkpoint.caption: Figure 2(d), cropped from the final paper without changing the plotted content.
checkpoint.body1: The same audit pipeline is applied to intermediate checkpoints. Attack AUC rises as training continues, indicating increasing membership risk.
checkpoint.body2: The scan can inform selection of a lower-risk checkpoint when utility is adequate. The page does not invent checkpoint values that the text does not report.
limits.title: Evidence the paper supports—and claims it does not establish
limits.not5: Universal transfer to arbitrary music models
limits.responsible: TS-RaMIA provides statistical auditing evidence and should be combined with provenance, licensing records, metadata, and other supporting evidence.
agent.kicker: Conceptual transfer / future direction — not evaluated in this paper
agent.title: From structured music auditing to structured Agent auditing
agent.map1_right: Tool calls / permission changes / external transmission / file writes
agent.map2_right: Trajectory length / tool count / task difficulty / user type
agent.map3_right: User-, task-, domain-, or attack-family-stratified splits
agent.map4_right: Detect unsafe actions without excessively blocking benign users
agent.transfers1: Audit the security-relevant parts of a structured sequence.
agent.transfers2: Control confounders before claiming an attack works.
agent.transfers3: Evaluate at deployment-relevant low false-positive rates.
agent.transfers4: Separate exploratory scores from calibrated decisions.
agent.transfers5: Use group-aware splits to prevent evaluation leakage.
agent.not1: Membership inference is not prompt-injection detection.
agent.not2: Symbolic-music structure is not identical to Agent semantics.
agent.not3: The paper does not evaluate Tool Use, RAG, Memory, or mobile-device actions.
agent.not4: Production systems may not expose token log-probabilities.
agent.not5: The proposed Agent extension is future work.
agent.future_label: Possible research direction — not a result of this paper
agent.future: A structure-aware audit for Agent trajectories could mask high-risk events such as tool invocation, permission escalation, external communication, and persistent-memory writes, then control trajectory length and task difficulty before measuring safety leakage at low FPR.

focus.title3: A strong raw AUC may be measuring structural complexity
focus.title4: Membership leakage is localized; uniform averages dilute it
focus.direction_warning_body: A single high or low raw NLL is not automatically a membership probability.
focus.method2: Length matching and calibration remove spurious correlations.
focus.method3: Composer-stratified out-of-fold evaluation reduces stylistic leakage.
focus.title6: Performance at the strict low-FPR operating point
focus.falsification1b: Windowed p95 adds a small lift.
focus.falsification2a: Note-only is unusable without score inversion.
focus.falsification3a: NotaGen under distribution shift—not a direct replication.
focus.falsification4a: The method requires per-token probabilities; generation-only API performance is not established.
